column11: the realised Medicare price of the therapy this study is trying to beat, in this exact disease, measured. Syfovre (pegcetacoplan), the first therapy approved for geographic atrophy, took $403,855,394.80 from CMS Medicare Part B over 29,338 beneficiaries in 2024, the book's own drug_demand table (asset row Syfovre, part B, year 2024): $13,765.61 a beneficiary. Part B pays 106% of the average sales price (Social Security Act section 1847A), so the price net of the add-on is $13,765.61 / 1.06 = $12,986.42. The same Syfovre series is already the anchor for this layer's penetration_peak_pct in regn_veopoz.csv, so the price and the reach are now measured on one product and one file. This row is written on the indication rather than on the asset, which forecast.layer_terms reads through LAYER_PRICE_KEYS, because the asset's own price is not this price: see the note
column12: A COMPARATOR, NOT A PRICE THIS PRODUCT HAS, AND THE CHOICE IS THE WHOLE OF THE JUDGEMENT. Veopoz's own price is published and it is two orders of magnitude higher: CMS OPPS Addendum B for October 2026 (effective 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31) carries 'J9376 Inj pozelimab-bbfg, 1 mg K 0911 91.73', a payment limit of $91.73 a milligram, and a dated press report of the launch price agrees to the cent at the 6% add-on, 'Regeneron has set a price of $34,612 per one-use vial for the once-weekly drug - equivalent to around $1.8 million a year at full price' (pharmaphorum, Phil Taylor, 2023-08-21), since $34,612 over 400 mg is $86.53 a milligram and $86.53 x 1.06 = $91.73. At the label's 10 mg/kg weekly maintenance that is millions a patient-year. THAT PRICE CANNOT CROSS INTO THIS INDICATION. It is set for CD55-deficient protein-losing enteropathy, a disease with a few dozen patients in the world, and the layer's own pool is 312,018 Americans. No payer funds an orphan price across a pool that size, and the regimen is different too: NCT06541704 gives pozelimab subcutaneously in combination with cemdisiran, or cemdisiran alone, not the 30 mg/kg intravenous load and 10 mg/kg weekly the Veopoz label describes. No price for that regimen is published anywhere. So the class price is taken. WHICH WAY IT ERRS: low, on two counts. Syfovre's 2024 was its second year on sale and its per-beneficiary spend was still climbing ($4,401.72 in 2023 on 17,414 beneficiaries), so a full year of treatment costs more than $13,765.61. And a systemic subcutaneous regimen that treats both eyes at once should command more than an intravitreal injection priced per eye, not less

column12: ICER's rate traces to Jalbert JJ, Chaudhari U, Zhang H, Weyne J, Shammo JM, Blood 2019;134(Supplement_1):3407 (doi 10.1182/blood-2019-125867), 1.3 per 100,000 in Truven MarketScan 2017 on n=257, which on the 324,985,539 US residents at 1 July 2017 gives 4,225 - within 2% of ICER's figure, so the two agree. BE AWARE JALBERT IS A CONFERENCE ABSTRACT, not a peer-reviewed paper; it is nonetheless the primary citation beneath every '12 to 13 per million' figure in circulation. DO NOT substitute the 2.4 per 100,000 from Tantravahi SK et al., J Health Econ Outcomes Res 2025;12(2):66-74 (doi 10.36469/001c.142049, PMID 40827257, PMC12358179): that is a FIVE-YEAR PERIOD prevalence among commercially insured under-65s, not a point prevalence, and the paper gives no national denominator

column12: THE SOFTEST ROW IN THIS FILE. Same conference-abstract caveat as the prevalence row, and worse: most high-quality international incidence studies cluster at 0.17 to 0.35 per 100,000 a year, a half to a third of this. Against a 4,303 prevalence it implies an average disease duration of 2.3 years, which is far too short for a chronic clonal disorder now managed with complement inhibitors - so either the incidence is too high or the prevalence too low, and the pair should not be read as internally consistent

column11: the transfused share, which is how ICER itself defines complement-inhibitor eligibility. Schrezenmeier H, Roth A, Araten DJ et al., 'Baseline clinical characteristics and disease burden in patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH): updated analysis from the International PNH Registry', Ann Hematol 2020;99(7):1505-1514 (doi 10.1007/s00277-020-04052-z, PMID 32390114, PMC7316848): 'In general, 61.3% (2219/3620) of patients had a history of RBC transfusions.' ICER applies it as exactly this: 'the percentage of patients with PNH who are symptomatic and eligible for a C5i (61.3%, assuming that the percentage of patients who are symptomatic are those with a history of RBC transfusions)'. 4,303 x 0.613 = 2,637
column12: a narrower, more mechanistic cut exists in the same registry if a human wants it: 1,173 of 3,620 (32.4%) had a GPI-deficient granulocyte clone of 50% or more, of whom 63.7% were transfused and 89.0% had LDH at 1.5x the upper limit of normal or above. ICER's 61.3% is used because it is the share ICER's own published chain uses, and that chain is reproducible: 4,303 x 0.613 x 0.21 = 554, which is exactly ICER's published '554 treatment experienced patients in the US over five years'

column11: ANCHOR, MEASURED, then a judgement multiple. The class capture: 30.0% of diagnosed US PNH patients had at least one complement inhibitor claim over 2018 to 2022 - eculizumab 16.4%, ravulizumab 21.9%, pegcetacoplan 2.2% (Tantravahi SK et al., J Health Econ Outcomes Res 2025;12(2):66-74, doi 10.36469/001c.142049, PMID 40827257, PMC12358179, commercial claims). On the prevalence above that is 4,303 x 0.30 = 1,291 treated, which against this layer's 2,637 eligible patients is 48.96% of the eligible pool already on a complement inhibitor. MULTIPLE 0.25, A JUDGEMENT, the multiple azn_azd7798.csv, azn_rilvegostomig.csv and lly_solbinsiran.csv all apply to an entrant displacing an established class: 0.489571 x 0.25 = 0.122393, about 323 patients at peak
column12: THE MULTIPLE IS THE MOST ARGUABLE NUMBER HERE and 0.25 is generous on its face: pozelimab plus cemdisiran would enter behind eculizumab, ravulizumab, pegcetacoplan, iptacopan, danicopan and crovalimab. For it: NCT05744921 is a Phase 3 in 202 patients, recruiting, and the combination's differentiator is a subcutaneous C5 regimen against infused incumbents, which is the axis ravulizumab used to take share from eculizumab. Against it: the anchor mixes sources - a commercial-claims treated share laid on a Medicare-inclusive prevalence - and no free source gives a clean US count of complement-inhibitor-treated PNH patients, because CMS Part B does not split eculizumab or ravulizumab beneficiaries across their four approved indications
